+title: A fork goes through the host launcher, so the host gives its surface before the first prompt runs (D205)
+---
+## Goal
+
+A fork that the `sessions` tool makes (`fork session`) runs on the tools of the source, and its first prompt starts at once. When a client later resumes the fork, the host stops the live fork and restores it on its own surface (the MCP servers and directories of the client or of the source). That stop can cancel the first prompt, and the first prompt ran on the wrong surface. Request from foundationmodelsacpagent-9e (D205).
+
+## Decision
+
+The Router already asks the host to build a session through `SessionLauncher` (`Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Directory/SessionLauncher.swift:39`) for `startAgent` and for a restore. A fork uses the same way:
+- Add a launcher operation for a fork, for example `forkSession(_ request: SessionLaunchForkRequest) async throws -> any RoutedSession`, with the source id, the cut position, and the fork id that the directory chose. Give it a default implementation that keeps the current behavior (the Router builds the fork with the tools of the source), so a launcher that does not implement it compiles.
+- `RouterSessionDirectory.fork(_:)` calls the launcher operation when the directory has a launcher, so the host builds the fork with its surface. Then the directory registers the fork and mails the first prompt. Thus no prompt runs before the host gave the surface, and the host holds the fork from its start (no stop and restore).
+- Keep the record, the recording node, the name, the hooks and the cut rule of ^3hxcxee.
+- Write the rule in the doc of `fork(_:)` and of the launcher operation.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] With a launcher that implements the fork operation: the launcher gets one call with the source, the cut position and the fork id; the fork uses the session that the launcher gave; the first prompt runs on that session.
+- [ ] With a launcher that does not implement it: the fork works as before.
+- [ ] The first prompt does not start before the launcher returns.
+- [ ] A launcher that throws: the fork is refused, nothing is registered, no recording node stays.
+
+## After
+
+Push when green. Send the sha and the name of the launcher operation to foundationmodelsacpagent-9e. #d205
\ No newline at end of file

+> 2 file(s) not reviewed — excluded by an ignore rule:

+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsRouterPublicSurfaceTests/SessionLauncherPublicSurfaceTests.swift:47` `reuse/reuse` — The new ForkingHostLauncher declares launchRootSession and restoreSession with bodies that are the same as the existing AgentlessLauncher stubs (both throw the same error). The new type repeats that stub behavior instead of reusing it, so a later change to the stub must be made in two places. Only the forkSession operation is new behavior here. Give AgentlessLauncher the forkSession operation as a parameter (for example, a closure with a default that throws), or let ForkingHostLauncher wrap or extend AgentlessLauncher, so only the fork operation is written in the new type.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsRouterTests/Helpers/ForkLauncherFixtures.swift:169` `reuse/reuse` — ForkLaunchingLauncher repeats the launchRootSession and restoreSession stub bodies (each throws Refusal) that the public-surface test launchers already implement. These two new stubs add a second copy of the same no-op behavior. Reuse one stub source for the no-op launcher operations. For example, move the shared no-op operations into one test helper that the fork launcher and the public-surface launcher both use, and keep only forkSession in ForkLaunchingLauncher.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Directory/SessionLaunchForkRequest.swift:169` `orchestrator-check/request-after-fork` — `ForkBuild` has no closed state, so the request stays usable after `RouterSessionDirectory.fork(_:)` ends. When the fork call ends with no fork built (the launcher throws before it builds, or it gives another session), the state stays `.open`. A launcher that kept the request (it is `Sendable` and public) can then call `makeFork()` or `makeFork(tools:)` later: this makes a second, live fork with a recording node in the folder of the source, with the tools of the source, that the directory does not register, hold or close. Also, a build that the launcher starts in a task of its own and that ends after the launcher threw is not discarded, because `discard()` (line 156) saw no fork. And a kept request keeps the source and its tools alive. Close the build when the fork call ends: for example, a `.closed` state that `launchFork(_:)` (`RouterSessionDirectory.swift:1512`) sets on each path (success and refusal), that `make(tools:)` refuses with a `SessionLaunchForkError`, and that discards a fork that a build in flight makes after the close. Drop the strong reference to the source at the close. Add tests: a request kept after a refused fork cannot build; a build that ends after the launcher threw leaves no live fork and no recording node.
